newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's AMP plans A$400 mln trust - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's AMP plans A$400 mln trust - paper.

text.p: Insurer and institutional investor The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) will launch on Monday a A$400 million property trust to be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange, The Sydney Morning Herald reported.
The trust would own shares in six large office towers in the Australian state capitals, the newspaper said, quoting from AMP national property sales and investment manager Neil Werrett.
"Fifty percent of the trust's assets will be in Sydney and North Sydney, where we believe the market is performing the best," Werrett was quoted as saying.
The Sydney Morning Herald said the AMP Office Trust would raise A$176.4 million in equity from the public through the issue of 185.6 million units at 95 cents each, fully underwritten by SBC Warburg.

"In addition AMP will retain A$132.6 milion worth of units or 37.5 percent of the trust, while Government of Singapore Investment Corp will hold A$33.5 million worth of units or 9.9 percent of the trust," the newspaper said.
"The expected market capitalisation of the trust on listing will be A$342.45 million," it said.
The trust would be geared to 17.3 percent of total assets or A$70 million and management had vowed to keep gearing under 25 percent.
SBC Warburg executive director John Carter told the Herald the trust would offer an annualised 1997 yield of 8.1 percent, rising to 8.6 percent in 1999.

The trust would own quarter shares of NAB House in Sydney and Bourke Place in Melbourne, a half share in the soon-to-be redeveloped American Express Tower in Sydney, The Gold Tower in Brisbane and 111 Alinga Street in Canberra.
"The trust will draw down another A$70 million in debt to fund the Amex development as needed," the Herald said.
At this stage the units would list on the Australian Stock Exchange on December 12.
